references.text: Isaiah describes how the people did not turn to the Lord even after discipline, reflecting the theme in Leviticus of refusing correction.
Jeremiah laments that the people refused to accept discipline, the same theme as the warning in Leviticus against rejecting rebuke.
Jeremiah describes a people who did not listen to the voice of the Lord and would not accept discipline, paralleling the warning in Leviticus.
Proverbs teach about the importance of accepting the Lord's discipline, which stands in contrast to the warning in Leviticus against rejecting it.
Amos describes repeated punishments from God where the people still did not turn back, illustrating the consequences of refusing correction.
Jeremiah says that the people would not accept discipline, directly reflecting the situation described in Leviticus 26:23.
Hebrews speaks of the Lord's discipline as a sign of love and warns against despising it, consistent with the warning in Leviticus.
